A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the potential reach of SMS-based health interventions is much higher than that of emails, and it is also higher than that of traditional mass media.

the use of mHealth for health education programs should be tailored to the specific population under study, and should take into account differences in access to and use of mobile phones, smartphones, and the Internet, as well as differences in willingness to receive SMS and email messages.

traditional mass media (radio and television) are the most cost effective way of reaching large populations in developing countries, while mHealth (SMS) has the potential to reach younger, more educated, and more affluent individuals, and thus may be more effective for specific groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the reach of mHealth interventions is not universal and that the potential reach varies across demographic and socioeconomic groups.

, although traditional mass media reach a large proportion of the population, mHealth may reach those with the most to gain from preventive health interventions, such as young adults and those in a high socioeconomic group.
mHealth has a greater potential for reaching the younger and more educated population in the Seychellois population than public television and radio.
